headline_marked: Ctg-M'singh rail link snapped as [[Bijoy Express engine catches fire]]
headline: Ctg-M'singh rail link snapped as Bijoy Express engine catches fire
summary: A locomotive fire near Atharbari station disabled the train, disrupting services on the Chattogram-Mymensingh route.
details: A fire broke out in the engine of the Bijoy Express this evening near Atharbari railway station in Mymensingh. The locomotive became disabled, causing a sudden halt to train movement on the Chattogram-Mymensingh route.
The incident occurred around 5:45 PM as the Jamalpur-bound train was passing through the area, according to Mymensingh Railway Police Station OC Akhtar Hossain.
Smoke began billowing from the engine before it went dead, leaving passengers stranded. Railway authorities have since dispatched a replacement engine to resume the journey toward Jamalpur.
In a separate incident earlier today, the coupling hook of the Jamalpur Express snapped in Gafargaon upazila, halting services on the Dhaka-Mymensingh route for over two hours.
The Jamalpur Express resumed its journey at approximately 2:30 PM after a replacement engine was provided to the disabled train.

headline_marked: BD entrepreneurs can [[sell goods on Amazon, eBay]] via new central bank rule
headline: BD entrepreneurs can sell goods on Amazon, eBay via new central bank rule
summary: Bangladesh Bank has introduced a regulated framework allowing domestic sellers to reach international buyers directly through global e-commerce platforms.
details: Bangladeshi entrepreneurs can now sell their products directly to foreign buyers through global online marketplaces like Amazon, eBay, AliExpress, Temu, and Flipkart.
Bangladesh Bank issued a notification on Monday introducing a regulated framework for these transactions, setting a maximum limit of $5,000 per transaction.
To ease documentation for micro exporters, the central bank has scrapped the Export Permit Certificate (EXP) requirement for shipments valued up to $1,000.
All export transactions must be routed through authorised dealer (AD) branches of commercial banks, which will verify valid agreements between exporters and marketplaces.
Entrepreneurs are also permitted to pay annual subscription fees for these online marketplaces through official banking channels.
Transactions will be settled through exporters’ foreign currency accounts (ERQ), with local currency accounts used for refunds if foreign currency is insufficient.
The central bank stated that this framework is designed to integrate local entrepreneurs into global e-commerce supply chains and facilitate small-value exports.
caption:
Selling on Amazon and eBay is now official for BD entrepreneurs! 🚀

Bangladeshi entrepreneurs can now sell their products directly to foreign buyers through global online marketplaces like Amazon, eBay, AliExpress, Temu, and Flipkart.

Bangladesh Bank issued a notification on Monday introducing a regulated framework for these transactions, setting a maximum limit of $5,000 per transaction.

To ease documentation for micro exporters, the central bank has scrapped the Export Permit Certificate (EXP) requirement for shipments valued up to $1,000.

All export transactions must be routed through authorised dealer (AD) branches of commercial banks, which will verify valid agreements between exporters and marketplaces.

Entrepreneurs are also permitted to pay annual subscription fees for these online marketplaces through official banking channels.

Transactions will be settled through exporters’ foreign currency accounts (ERQ), with local currency accounts used for refunds if foreign currency is insufficient.

The central bank stated that this framework is designed to integrate local entrepreneurs into global e-commerce supply chains and facilitate small-value exports.
